result.topic_en: Differential relations for the perturbation of longitude and latitude in terms of element variations, followed by the relations connecting an initial state (position and velocity) of a heavenly body with its orbital elements.
result.transcription:
57.
$\partial l = \mathcal{E}.\partial Ep. + (n\mathcal{E} - \frac{2rA}{\partial 7})\partial 7 + (\mathcal{B}-\mathcal{E})\partial\varpi + \mathcal{F}\partial\varphi + C\partial i + (\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{B})\partial\Omega$
$\partial b = \mathcal{E}'\partial Ep. + (n\mathcal{E}' - \frac{2rA'}{\partial 7})\partial 7 + (\mathcal{B}'-\mathcal{E}')\partial\varpi + \mathcal{F}'\partial\varphi + C'\partial i + (\mathcal{D}'-\mathcal{B}')\partial\Omega$

Zusammenhang des Initialzustandes
mit den Elementen.
$r$... Radius Vector
$v$... Länge in der Bahn
$\lambda$... Länge in der Ekliptik
$b$... Breite
$\Omega$... Länge des aufsteigenden Knotens
$i$... Neigung der Bahn
$e = \sin\varphi$ Excentricität, $p$ halber Parameter
$\omega$... Perihelium
$t$.... Zeit
$k$..... Constante $= \sqrt{\Theta}$

1) $\tang b = \tang i \sin(\lambda - \Omega)$
2) $\frac{\partial b}{\cos b^2 \partial\lambda} = \tang i \cos(\lambda - \Omega)$
3) $\frac{rr dv}{k dt} = \sqrt{p}$
4) $\frac{r^3 \partial v^2}{\Theta \partial t^2} - 1 = e\cos(v-\omega)$
5) $\frac{rr dr dv}{\Theta dt^2} = e\sin(v-\omega)$
6) $\frac{2}{r} - \frac{rr dv^2 + dr^2}{\Theta dt^2} = \frac{1}{a}$
7) $2 \mathrm{Arc.tg} \sqrt{\frac{1-e}{1+e}}.\mathrm{tg}\frac{1}{2}v - \frac{e\sqrt{(1-ee)}\sin v}{1+e\cos v} - k\int\frac{\partial t}{a^{\frac{3}{2}}} = \varepsilon - \omega$

methods.what: Linear differential expression of the change in longitude in terms of variations of the orbital elements (epoch, mean motion-related quantity, perihelion, eccentricity angle, inclination, node)
Analogous differential expression for the change in latitude
Latitude in terms of inclination and longitude from the node
Derivative of latitude with respect to longitude, determining inclination and node from the direction of motion
Area law: angular momentum gives the semi-parameter
Eccentricity and perihelion from radius and angular velocity (cosine component)
Eccentricity and perihelion from radial and angular velocity (sine component)
Vis-viva equation giving the semi-major axis
Kepler's equation in terms of true anomaly, determining the mean longitude at epoch
